author: reek
body: An idle core halts instead of busy-spinning, and is woken again to pick up work. This is the workload that exercises the wake path hardest: the boot program spawns one child at a time and waits on it, so between cycles three of four cores have nothing to run and halt on `hlt`. Each cycle the boot program itself blocks in `process-wait`, its core halts, the child runs on another core and exits, the exit wake loop marks the waiter READY, and a halted core must wake from its timer, scan, and resume it.

author: reek
body: A lost wake anywhere in that chain -- a waiter that commits to BLOCKED after the child's exit already scanned past it, a half-built spawn claimed before its slice is set, an idle core that halts and is never woken -- shows up as a hang: one of the waits never returns and the final line never prints. The spin is sized so the child outlives a scheduling tick, so the waiter really does block and its core really does halt rather than finding the child already done. Run it many times; a single hang is a failure.
